It took a little while for people to figure out where to find everything added in the DLC. FromSoft did what FromSoft does and snuck them into places you wouldn't expect. But now that everyone feels like they've found it all, including some minor additions that weren't announced, the testing has begun. By far the most popular new weapon is a greatsword you can steal from a new NPC who can show up for a duel. Leontiel's Greatsword is a direct reference to a character from Dark Souls 2 and comes with a powerful new move that mimics real life bullfighters, or matadors. title: I tried the sequel to Task Manager and it has too many special effects
summary: If Task Manager is so good, why isn't there a Task Manager 2?
body: The original Task Manager (that program you only ever open when something has gone wrong in your rig) originally launched way back in 1995. Now, 31 years later, its creator has put out a follow-up. About time, I know. Dave Plummer, former Microsoft Engineer turned YouTuber turned guy who really wants you to know he made Task Manager, has just released Task Manager OG , and it works on Windows, Linux, and Mac. Plummer says he wrote a 107-page spec, fed it to Claude, and then partly vibe-coded this new program while his kid was getting surgery. "By the time he was out of the hospital, I had a rough app working. But then he started bleeding internally, needed emergency surgery and a blood transfusion. Happy to say he's all better now—but suffice to say I had the rest of the week to tinker as he healed." Now, with much better hardware than users had back in the '90s, Plummer wanted a Task Manager that would "push the limits." The sequel software animates at 60 Hz and provides data like mouse tracking and a summary page. title: Chinese memory maker YMTC wants to dethrone Samsung and SK hynix by the end of 2027
summary: YMTC has some big plans.
body: With the memory crisis in full swing, it's taking severe chunks out of the supplies of both NAND (used for SSD storage) and DRAM, which is used for RAM modules. Chinese memory maker YMTC has had a lucrative couple of years with the former, yet it's not done yet. YMTC reportedly wants to sit at the very top of the pile for NAND flash memory, and it wants to do it very soon. According to the Financial Times , citing "two people with knowledge of the matter", YMTC told investors that it wants to be the leader in the market (ahead of Samsung and SK hynix) by the end of 2027. That's a pretty bold claim considering it would need to more than double its current market share. According to Counterpoint Research , YMTC holds a 13% market share, while NAND memory leader Samsung holds 29%. In fairness, though, YMTC does appear to be building up its infrastructure to handle growth. In April, it was reported that YMTC was aiming to more than double its wafer production . It would do so by building two additional foundries and finishing the build of a third foundry that was already under construction. NAND memory is a very lucrative business right now. title: Pulsar's new mouse is sliced in half to make it genuinely 'crazy-light'
summary: 'I swear it came like that,' I say as I chew through half a mouse.
body: With mice sensors getting so ludicrously high-spec'd, some competitive gaming mouse brands are instead trying to make the shell as light as possible. Lighter = speedier. And Pulsar is finally joining the uber-lightweight mouse trend, with a 29 gram gaming mouse that is, well, half of a mouse. Effectively, the new X2F CrazyLight is just the front half of a gaming mouse, including the sensors, switches, and battery. Pulsar is not the first to cut a gaming mouse in half (in fact, the G-Wolves HSK Pro V2.0 has been around for a while and is just 26.8 g). It's not even the first very light gaming mouse from Pulsar, with the X2 CrazyLight Mini being 35 g, but it is the lightest ever Pulsar mouse, to my knowledge. And it manages to get that weight without going for the honeycomb shell that many other lightweight competitors go for. According to Pulsar , the new X2F comes kitted with Pulsar's new SX2 sensor, which we don't currently have the stats for. The previous generation XS1 has a DPI of up to 32,000, a max speed of 750 IPS, and acceleration of 50 G. This is the sensor our Jacob Fox had his mitts on when he reviewed the X2 CrazyLight Medium and X3 Crazylight Mini . It also supports u…

title: After seeing what GTA 6 does to a PS5 we're even more desperate to see what the PC version has for us
summary: Looking at the PlayStation 5 capture, we're noodling on just what extra shinies Rockstar might add to the best gaming platform's version.
body: So GTA 6 officially slammed into our collective eyeballs last night with a full 26 minutes of pure gameplay (well, that and some cutscenes) and it has made us ever more desperate to get our hands on a proper PC build of the game. But the hardware team has been poring over the released footage captured on a lowly PlayStation 5 and we've put our heads together to figure out what we think, and what extra bells and whistly things we want to see built into the eventual PC build of the game. For right now, we have an admittedly beautifully looking game running at a peasant 30 fps frame rate, on a seven year-old Sony console. The top PC hardware of today is far beyond what the aging hardware inside the PS5 is capable of… even if right now the cost of admittance to the world of top PC hardware is inexcusably high. Who knows, maybe by the time GTA 6 is allowed to release on PC the RAMpocalypse will be over? Though that either means GTA 6 won't release on PC until maybe 2031 or the AI bubble pops sending us back into the economic stone age. Cheery thought. title: Netflix is likely pleased as punch with the GTA 6 extended look, which more than doubled its web traffic
summary: Done deal.
body: One of the more confusing elements of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look is the fact that it debuted on Netflix, of all sites. Why? While it's harder to pin down the reasons Take-Two went for it, I can at least suss out that Netflix is probably feeling very happy with its end of the bargain. That's per GamesBeat , which pulled the numbers from Sensor Tower, a market intelligence firm. According to them, the average user count on mobile increased by 50% when compared to the past 12 Thursdays—meanwhile, the average web user count went up a stonking 125%. This was enough of a bump to cause issues for some viewers , though Netflix otherwise held up reasonably well . That's great news for the streaming platform, which has presumably been struggling to keep up with that ever-enshittifying perpetual growth mindset—introducing ads over the past few years, ramping up prices, and toying with generative AI to make those aforementioned ads even more annoying. We can, sadly, expect more of this in the future. As for what Take-Two got out of it, it's hard to say, given CEO Strauss Zelnick has been tight-lipped on the particulars . title: The GTA 6 reveal has me wowed by Vice City and underwhelmed by Rockstar's same old missions
summary: Looks like we're in for more Rockstar missions, for better and worse.
body: The big gameplay reveal for GTA 6 has come and gone, and I'm surprised by how mixed I am on it. In some ways, I'm more excited than ever play it. Vice City gives an amazing first impression—I'm already convinced it'll be the special sort of open world that you just want to exist in. Rockstar is packing it full of little activities and human touches that might make GTA 6 a borderline life sim: eating, drinking, sleeping, recreation, hanging out with buds, skydiving, dirt bike racing, and store robbing (I didn't say the activities were all aspirational). I'm seeing a lot of stuff I want to do. That stuff looks so good it's almost overwhelming, but the bits in between all that—those fragments of story missions—were less impressive. I was hoping 13 years would change the shape of GTA's authored action, but Rockstar is still very much working with the same tools. In the first mission we see Jason and Lucia doing a drug deal for Boobie Ike, and I bet you can guess what happens: The pair exchange some uneasy words with the buyer, then the deal goes wrong when the cops show up. title: Holy crap, it's happening: Dwarf Fortress gets its first Myth and Magic update later this year, bringing each player's world its own procedural magic system
summary: "Everything that makes fantasy what it is—with every piece tied into how that particular universe works, down to its bones."
body: Even as it achieved fractal complexity by modeling feline alcohol poisoning, procedural bardic traditions, and delayed-action thermonuclear dragonfire , the creators of Dwarf Fortress—brothers Tarn and Zach Adams—have maintained still loftier ambitions for their legendary fantasy sim. In recent years, that effort has been guided by one goal: Creating magic. Procedural, universe-specific magic, interwoven with the unique cosmology and mythology modeled each and every time the player clicks the "create new world" button. For a game already setting a high watermark for simulational complexity, it's an incredibly ambitious endeavor. It's taken a decade. It's demanded a complete scripting overhaul, aided by the heroic effort of Bay 12 Games' first non-Adams programmer , Putnam. Frankly, it's almost strained believability. And it'll start arriving later this year. Tarn Adams confirmed that Dwarf Fortress' first Myth and Magic update will land before the end of the year in a short announcement video , embedded above. title: Almost 20 years later, Arkane's founder says he understands why Valve cancelled the Ravenholm game that never was: 'It all came down to the economics'
summary: "We grew up and got a little bit more mature about it."
body: One of the quiet tragedies of Valve's game library is a standalone Ravenholm game that never came to fruition—it was being worked on by Arkane Studios in the late 2000s, and it would've probably been pretty damn good if Valve had the moolah to make it. Over a decade later, an entire hour of footage would drop online , with reports stating that around 10 levels had been fleshed out prior. Now, almost 20 years later, Arkane's founder Raphaël Colantonio has managed to find his zen with the heartbreak, speaking with Press Box PR in an interview earlier this month (thanks, GamesRadar+ ). "It took us a decade to move on from the pain of the Ravenholm project because we were incredibly excited about doing that game and we put in a lot of creative energy into it and eventually when the decision was made to cut it, we did not understand it as it happened," said Colantonio. "We were young and we were just refusing to see the reality of the situation, and the reality was much simpler than the way it looked to us." title: What's the best starting class in Star Wars Zero Company?
summary: Pick a decent specialization to begin with.
body: Picking the best starting class in Star Wars Zero Company is a little challenging when you haven't played any of the game yet. But don't worry: you can change your class specialization once you hit Cycle 3, which is very early on. After that point, you can also change the specialization and talents for hired operators too. The only thing you can't tweak is named character talents, like Hawk's Fearless Leader. Below I'll offer my recommendation for the best starting specialization in Star Wars Zero Company, plus some options if you don't want to double-up classes with any of the named characters you initially team-up with. Star Wars Zero Company best starting class There are eight specializations to choose from (Image credit: Bit Reactor) The best starting class in Star Wars Zero Company is the Scoundrel . This specialization has a great kit focused around making enemies vulnerable (for guaranteed critical hits), penetrating their defenses, and increased assist damage. This ties in perfectly to Hawk's Fearless Leader talent, which increases assist damage for the whole squad when they're present. title: The best talents for each specialization in Star Wars Zero Company
summary: Pick the perfect talent to go with each class.
body: Picking the best talents in Star Wars Zero Company is something you'll start pondering when you unlock recruitable operators in the game. Each of these will have both a class and a talent, but the good news is that you can respec both in the change specialization menu once you've recruited them. This means it's usually a better idea to recruit a character you like the look of, versus one with a talent you can tweak anyway. Some of these talents have a very clear and strong synergy with Zero Company's specializations, so I'll run through all available talents and talent levels below, plus give my top picks for each class.
